questions.question: Which company made Japan's first ball bearing?
questions.explanation: NSK, founded in 1916, was Japan's first bearing maker and produced the country's first ball bearings.

questions.question: Bearing '6205': what is the bore size?
questions.explanation: For bore codes 04 and above, multiply by 5: 05 × 5 = 25 mm.

questions.question: Suffix 'ZZ' on a bearing means?
questions.explanation: ZZ shows metal shields on both sides; DDU means contact rubber seals on both sides.

questions.question: Which bearing type carries mainly axial load?
questions.explanation: Thrust bearings are designed for loads acting along the shaft axis.

questions.question: Bore code '00' means a bore of?
questions.explanation: Special codes: 00 = 10 mm, 01 = 12 mm, 02 = 15 mm, 03 = 17 mm.

questions.question: Bore code '03' means a bore of?
questions.explanation: Codes 00–03 are fixed at 10, 12, 15 and 17 mm; from 04 onward multiply by 5.

questions.question: Which part keeps balls evenly spaced?
questions.explanation: The cage (retainer) separates and guides rolling elements so they do not rub together.

questions.question: C3 internal clearance versus Normal is?
questions.explanation: Order is C2 < CN < C3 < C4; C3 suits tight fits or high running temperature.

questions.question: Ball bearing life: L10 = (C/P) to power?
questions.explanation: For ball bearings the life exponent is 3; for roller bearings it is 10/3.

questions.question: Roller bearing life exponent is?
questions.explanation: Line contact of rollers gives a life exponent of 10/3 in the ISO 281 life equation.

questions.question: L10 life means what % of bearings survive?
questions.explanation: L10 is the life that 90% of identical bearings reach or exceed before fatigue flaking.

questions.question: Basic dynamic load rating symbol?
questions.explanation: C is the load giving a basic life of one million revolutions; C0 is the static rating.

questions.question: Halving load on a ball bearing raises life by?
questions.explanation: Life varies with (C/P)³, so halving the load gives 2³ = 8 times the life.

questions.question: Angular contact pair 'DB' means?
questions.explanation: DB (back-to-back) gives high moment rigidity; DF is face-to-face and DT is tandem.

questions.question: Which arrangement allows shaft thermal growth?
questions.explanation: A floating bearing at one end lets the shaft expand without heavy axial load.

questions.question: Preload in a bearing increases what?
questions.explanation: Preload removes internal clearance, raising stiffness and running accuracy.

questions.question: Ring rotating against load needs which fit?
questions.explanation: The ring rotating relative to the load needs an interference fit to prevent creep.

questions.question: Standard bearing steel is?
questions.explanation: High-carbon chromium steel (SUJ2/100Cr6) gives the hardness needed for rolling fatigue.

questions.question: Typical hardness of bearing rings?
questions.explanation: Through-hardened bearing steel is tempered to around 58–64 HRC for fatigue and wear resistance.

questions.question: Ceramic bearing balls are made of?
questions.explanation: Silicon nitride (Si3N4) balls are light, very hard and electrically insulating.

questions.question: Ceramic balls in EV motors prevent what?
questions.explanation: Insulating balls block stray current that causes fluting and pitting on raceways.

questions.question: Vacuum-degassed bearing steel reduces?
questions.explanation: Fewer oxide inclusions mean fewer crack starting points and longer fatigue life.

questions.question: Main microstructure after hardening?
questions.explanation: Quench and temper gives tempered martensite with fine carbides: hard and dimensionally stable.

questions.question: What does grease mainly do in a bearing?
questions.explanation: Lubricant separates rolling surfaces, cutting friction, wear and heat, and protects against rust.

questions.question: Grease stiffness is graded by?
questions.explanation: NLGI grades grease consistency; NLGI 2 is the most common grade for bearings.

questions.question: Oil viscosity grade system is called?
questions.explanation: ISO VG gives kinematic viscosity at 40 °C, for example ISO VG 68.

questions.question: EHL in bearing lubrication stands for?
questions.explanation: Elasto-hydrodynamic lubrication forms a thin oil film under very high contact pressure.

questions.question: Typical grease fill inside a bearing?
questions.explanation: Around one-third fill avoids churning heat; overfilling raises temperature and torque.

questions.question: Which test checks rust resistance?
questions.explanation: Salt spray (fog) testing exposes parts to saline mist to judge corrosion protection.

questions.question: The Anderon meter measures bearing?
questions.explanation: The Anderon meter measures vibration in low, medium and high bands to detect waviness and defects.

questions.question: Surface roughness is commonly shown as?
questions.explanation: Ra is the average roughness height of a surface, in micrometres.

questions.question: A CMM is used to check what?
questions.explanation: A Coordinate Measuring Machine probes parts to measure size, form and position.

questions.question: Which test finds surface cracks magnetically?
questions.explanation: Magnetic particle inspection shows surface and near-surface cracks in steel parts.

questions.question: Raceway roundness is checked with a?
questions.explanation: A roundness tester rotates the part against a probe to measure form error in microns.

questions.question: Bearing endurance testing confirms what?
questions.explanation: Life test rigs run bearings under load until flaking to confirm rated life.

questions.question: Flaking on a raceway is a sign of?
questions.explanation: Flaking is scaly peeling of the surface caused by rolling contact fatigue.

questions.question: Dents at ball spacing on a raceway mean?
questions.explanation: Brinelling comes from shock or wrong mounting force pushed through the rolling elements.

questions.question: Fluting (washboard marks) is caused by?
questions.explanation: Electric current passing through the bearing creates regular grooves called fluting.

questions.question: Fretting at the bore fit is caused by?
questions.explanation: Tiny relative movement between ring and shaft wears and oxidises the fit surface.

questions.question: Outer ring creep is usually due to?
questions.explanation: Too little interference lets the ring slowly turn on its seat, wearing the fit.

questions.question: FEA is used to predict what?
questions.explanation: Finite Element Analysis simulates stress and deformation before prototypes are made.

questions.question: CAD stands for?
questions.explanation: CAD software creates 2D drawings and 3D models of bearings and parts.

questions.question: GD&T on drawings controls what?
questions.explanation: Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing defines allowed form, orientation and location.

questions.question: DFMEA analyses risks in what?
questions.explanation: Design FMEA finds possible failure modes of the product design and their causes.

questions.question: How many phases does APQP have?
questions.explanation: APQP: planning, product design, process design, validation, and feedback/corrective action.

questions.question: DVP&R: Design Verification Plan &?
questions.explanation: The DVP&R lists tests needed to prove a design and records their results.

questions.question: EV motor bearings mostly need what?
questions.explanation: E-motors spin very fast, so bearings need low friction, high-speed cages and insulation.

questions.question: Gen-3 hub unit integrates what?
questions.explanation: Gen-3 hub units integrate the wheel and body flanges, cutting weight and assembly time.

questions.question: Most precise ISO bearing tolerance class?
questions.explanation: ISO classes tighten from Normal (0) through 6, 5 and 4 to class 2, the most precise.

questions.question: The 'dmn' value rates bearing?
questions.explanation: dmn = pitch diameter (mm) × speed (rpm), a common index of bearing speed capability.
